name: access-canary
purpose: Proves on every release that readers see only tested rows, with their role's policy applied: five synthetic rows that each canary principal sees differently, read through the reader view governance.access_canary.events.
limitations: Synthetic, and useful for nothing else. Its event times are the build's own clock minus each seed row's age, so they move with every build: the delay proof needs a build that passed in the last 19 minutes, which the 10-minute schedule gives. A stale canary fails the delayed reader's expectation rather than passing it.
usage: At build, rows 1 (north) and 4 (south) are a day old, row 2 (north) 21 minutes, and rows 3 (north) and 5 (south) 1 minute. p.canary-full (full_reader) sees all five; p.canary-delayed (delayed_reader: delay 20 minutes on event_ts, note masked) sees 1, 2 and 4 with note null; p.canary-scoped (public_reader: row scope region north) sees 1, 2 and 3. Any other id is not from the seed, so it was never tested. Each is a row of tests/access/expectations.yaml.

outputs.purpose: One synthetic canary row per seed row, built so that each reader policy visibly changes what its canary principal reads: some rows younger than the delay, two regions, a note to mask.

columns.name: id
columns.description: The seed row's number, 1 to 5; a reader shown any other id was shown an untested row.

columns.name: region
columns.description: north or south; public_reader keeps north only. The partition source, so it is in the key, as an incremental build's unique key must hold every partition source column.

columns.name: note
columns.description: A marker a leak can be searched for, canary-note-<id>; delayed_reader reads it as null.

columns.name: event_ts
columns.description: The build's clock minus the seed row's age_minutes; delayed_reader sees a row only once this is 20 minutes old.

roles.inWords: only rows whose event_ts is at least 20 minutes old; note read as null
only rows whose region is north
